articles.title: FIR Filed Against 7 for Offering Namaz in Malegaon Municipal Office | MMC Controversy
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In Malegaon, police have registered a case against seven individuals for allegedly offering namaz inside the Electricity Department office of the Malegaon Municipal Corporation (MMC).

body.html:
In Malegaon, police have registered a case against seven individuals for allegedly offering namaz inside the Electricity Department office of the Malegaon Municipal Corporation (MMC).

The case was filed on February 25, 2026, at the Malegaon Quilla Police Station based on a complaint by Mahendra Raghunath Sawant (43), an MMC employee.

According to police, on February 23, a delegation led by Lukman Kamal, president of the Malegaon Lok Sangharsh Samiti, visited the MMC office to raise concerns over unresolved power supply issues in their ward. The group reportedly waited for several hours to meet officials. As the delay coincided with the Asr (afternoon) prayer time, they offered namaz inside the office premises, stating they did so to avoid missing their scheduled meeting.

Police have booked the individuals under multiple provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Maharashtra Police Act, including:

Section 132 (BNS): Use of criminal force against a public servant
Section 189 (BNS): Unlawful assembly
Section 190 (BNS): Joint liability of members of an unlawful assembly
Section 292 (BNS): Public nuisance

A video of the prayer inside the office circulated widely on social media, triggering protests from local BJP leaders and certain Hindu organisations. In response, activists associated with the Sakal Hindu Samaj reportedly recited the Hanuman Chalisa within the MMC premises as a form of protest.

Malegaon Municipal Commissioner Ravindra Jadhav has ordered a formal inquiry into the incident. Police said further investigation is underway.

articles.title: SHOCKING: Man Brutally Assaults Wife on Busy Road in Tonk, Rajasthan | Deoli Viral Video
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing video from Deoli town in Tonk district, Rajasthan, has sparked widespread outrage after it showed a man allegedly assaulting his wife in broad daylight on a busy road. The incident reportedly took place near a private nursing home on Jahazpur Chungi Naka Road.

body.html:
A disturbing video from Deoli town in Tonk district, Rajasthan, has sparked widespread outrage after it showed a man allegedly assaulting his wife in broad daylight on a busy road.

The incident reportedly took place near a private nursing home on Jahazpur Chungi Naka Road. In the viral footage, the husband is seen riding a motorcycle and attempting to forcibly make his wife sit on it by dragging her by the hair. The woman can be heard protesting and crying in pain as the man repeatedly pulls her and tries to force her onto the vehicle.

Eyewitness accounts suggest that the altercation continued for nearly 15–20 minutes. During this time, several passersby gathered at the spot, but instead of intervening, many were seen recording the incident on their mobile phones.

At one point, both the man and the woman reportedly lost balance and fell onto the road along with the motorcycle. Despite the fall, the dispute continued briefly. The situation reportedly de-escalated only after some people at the scene threatened to call the police, following which the man left with his wife.

The identities of the couple and the exact reason behind the dispute have not yet been officially confirmed.

The video has triggered strong reactions on social media, with users expressing anger not only over the alleged assault but also over the apparent inaction of bystanders. The incident has reignited debate around public responsibility, bystander intervention, and societal apathy in cases of visible violence.

Authorities are expected to examine the viral clip and ascertain the facts surrounding the incident.

articles.title: SHOCKING: Mumbai Fruit Vendors Caught Using Rat Poison on Bananas | Malad News
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing food safety incident in Mumbai’s Malad area has triggered public outrage after two fruit vendors were allegedly caught applying rat poison to fruits meant for sale. The episode surfaced after a video recorded by local residents in Rajanpada went viral on social media.

body.html:
A disturbing food safety incident in Mumbai’s Malad area has triggered public outrage after two fruit vendors were allegedly caught applying rat poison to fruits meant for sale.

The episode surfaced after a video recorded by local residents in Rajanpada went viral on social media. In the clip, one of the vendors is seen holding a tube of Ratol poison while handling bananas. Bystanders are heard confronting him, questioning why poisonous substance was being applied to fruits consumed by children and families.

Following the viral footage, Malad Police acted swiftly. A local resident, Kunal Salunke, lodged a formal complaint around 9 pm, alleging that two fruit sellers were using rat poison on their produce, posing a serious public health risk. Based on the complaint, an FIR was registered and both vendors were detained.

The accused have been identified as Manoj Kumar Kesarwani and Bipin (Vipin) Kesarwani. During preliminary interrogation, they reportedly told police that the poison was being used to prevent rodents from damaging fruits in godowns and on carts. However, officials termed the act extremely hazardous and unlawful.

Police warned that applying rat poison to edible items could cause severe poisoning, organ failure and other life-threatening health complications.

A case has been registered under Sections 125, 274, 275 and 286 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. The shop has been sealed and further investigation is underway to determine whether similar practices were carried out earlier.

(According to reports incident occurred 24 Feb 2026 Thursday night)

articles.title: Speeding Innova Crushes Bike in Gurugram Jam, UP Youth Dies in Hospital
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A youth was killed after a speeding Innova rammed into a motorcycle stuck in a traffic jam on the Gurugram–Faridabad road near Gwal Pahari Chowki on February 23 evening.

body.html:
A youth was killed after a speeding Innova rammed into a motorcycle stuck in a traffic jam on the Gurugram–Faridabad road near Gwal Pahari Chowki on February 23 evening.

According to police, the accident occurred around 4:45 pm when two brothers, Mohammad Rashid and Shakir, were travelling from DLF Phase-3 to Dabua Colony in Faridabad. Amid heavy traffic near Gwal Pahari, an Innova car allegedly hit their motorcycle from behind. The impact pushed the bike into a parked car, leaving it wedged between the two vehicles.

Both brothers sustained serious injuries and were rushed to BK Hospital in Faridabad, where Shakir, a resident of Karamas Khedi village in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, died during treatment.

Based on Mohammad Rashid’s complaint, an FIR has been registered against the Innova driver at the DLF Phase-1 police station. Investigating officer ASI Karan said the vehicle has been seized and the driver will be served a notice to join the probe. Further action will be taken after investigation.

articles.title: Alleged Inflammatory Wall Message Sparks Alert; Ghaziabad Police Says Video Misleading
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The administration in Ghaziabad was placed on high alert after a viral video claimed that an offensive message targeting a particular community was written on a roadside wall ahead of Holi.

body.html:
The administration in Ghaziabad was placed on high alert after a viral video claimed that an offensive message targeting a particular community was written on a roadside wall ahead of Holi.

Video Goes Viral

A 59-second video circulating on social media shows a group of people, reportedly including women, writing a controversial message in large letters on a wall along the Delhi–Dehradun National Highway. Religious slogans can also be heard in the background.

The location was claimed to be near a tunnel area close to the Saharanpur district border. In the footage, a woman wearing a saffron scarf is seen writing on the wall, while others stand nearby. A man appears to be recording the incident. The message is painted in bold black and white letters.

Police Launch Probe

Following the circulation of the video, local police and administrative officials initiated an inquiry. Authorities inspected the site and alerted concerned police stations.

Police stated that the authenticity of the video is under verification and that those found involved would face legal action. Officials added that prima facie the act appeared intentional and potentially aimed at disturbing social harmony. Additional police personnel have been deployed as a precautionary measure.

Meanwhile, Pinky Chaudhary, national president of the Hindu Raksha Dal, reportedly claimed that the writing was done by members of her organisation, further intensifying the controversy. The group has faced previous scrutiny, including alleged involvement in an arms distribution case two months ago.

Police Clarification

However, the Ghaziabad Police issued a statement saying the video is misleading and that no such incident occurred within the jurisdiction of the Ghaziabad Police Commissionerate.

Authorities have appealed to the public not to share unverified or inflammatory content, especially during the festive season, warning that strict action will be taken against those attempting to spread rumours or disrupt communal harmony.

Technical examination of the viral video is ongoing, and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: 9-Year-Old Girl Collapses, Dies at Gotan International School in Nagaur district
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A nine-year-old girl died after suddenly collapsing during playtime at a private school in Rajasthan’s Nagaur district on February 23. The incident occurred around 7:48 am at Gotan International School in Gotan town.

body.html:
A nine-year-old girl died after suddenly collapsing during playtime at a private school in Rajasthan’s Nagaur district on February 23.

The incident occurred around 7:48 am at Gotan International School in Gotan town. The deceased, Divya, a Class 5 student and daughter of Rajendra Bapedia from Talanpur, had arrived at school as usual. With time remaining before the morning assembly, several students were playing on the school ground when she suddenly stumbled, fainted and fell.

School staff immediately rushed to her assistance and informed her family. She was taken to the Government Hospital in Gotan, where doctors declared her dead.

Suspected Cardiac Arrest

Doctors stated that there were no visible external injury marks on Divya’s body. In the preliminary assessment, cardiac arrest is suspected to be the cause of death.

The family declined a postmortem examination. After completing necessary formalities, the hospital handed over the body to the family.

School Director Ramkunwar Ola said the child had come to school normally and was playing before assembly when she unexpectedly collapsed.

Elder Brother Died in Similar Manner

Family members revealed that Divya’s elder brother, Abhishek, had also died under similar circumstances about four months ago. On September 9, 2025, he reportedly fainted while playing at home and was later declared dead at a hospital.

The consecutive deaths of two siblings within a short span have left the family and the local community in deep shock.

articles.title: Violent Protest at ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India Site in Hazira; Vehicles Torched
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major labour unrest broke out on Thursday, 26 February 2026, at the AM/NS project site in Hazira, Surat, involving nearly 5,000 contract workers deployed by Larsen & Toubro (L&T). What Triggered the Protest?

body.html:
A major labour unrest broke out on Thursday, 26 February 2026, at the AM/NS project site in Hazira, Surat, involving nearly 5,000 contract workers deployed by Larsen & Toubro (L&T).

What Triggered the Protest?

The workers alleged that they were being paid only ₹600–₹700 per day despite performing high-risk industrial work. They also demanded:

Reduction of duty hours from 12 hours to 8 hours

Wage revision in line with industry standards

Tensions escalated when the protest turned violent. An agitated mob allegedly set several vehicles, including cars and two-wheelers, on fire. Company assets such as fire engines and access-control systems were also reportedly damaged.

Police Action

To control the situation, Surat Police carried out a mild lathi-charge and fired between 35 and 70 tear gas shells to disperse the crowd. At least three police personnel, including a DCB inspector, sustained injuries during the clashes.

More than 25 workers have been detained. Police are in the process of registering FIRs, with some detainees likely to face serious charges, including attempt to murder.

Alleged Trigger Behind Escalation

According to a report by The Times of India, the unrest was reportedly fuelled by viral videos of a similar protest at an IOCL refinery in Panipat following a worker’s death, which heightened tensions among workers at the Hazira site.

Company Response

AM/NS India stated that L&T management is in dialogue with worker representatives to address the grievances and restore normalcy.

L&T, in a statement reported by The Week, said it will implement all provisions of the new labour code once notified by the Gujarat government.

Authorities have deployed additional security at the site, and investigations are ongoing to assess the full extent of the damage and identify those responsible for the violence.

articles.title: Bride Walks Out of Wedding in Hamirpur district, Chooses Lover Hours After Marriage
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a dramatic development from Uttar Pradesh, a newly married woman in Hamirpur district ended her marriage just hours after the ceremony, stating that she wished to live with her lover instead of her husband. According to police, the wedding took place on Saturday morning.

body.html:
In a dramatic development from Uttar Pradesh, a newly married woman in Hamirpur district ended her marriage just hours after the ceremony, stating that she wished to live with her lover instead of her husband.

According to police, the wedding took place on Saturday morning. However, shortly after the rituals were completed, the bride reportedly informed her husband and in-laws that she was in love with another man and did not wish to continue the marriage. A video clip that has surfaced online shows a confrontation inside the house, where the mother-in-law is allegedly seen assaulting the bride after she refused to accept the marriage and declined the ‘suhaag raat’.

Family members alerted the police following the dispute. Officials said the woman clearly stated before authorities and villagers that she had married under circumstances she no longer accepted and wanted to stay with the man she loved.

Police Intervention

Local police intervened and held discussions with both families and the couple. After confirming that both individuals were adults and that the woman was unwilling to continue the relationship, an application was reportedly processed to formalise the separation. Police stated that consent was a key factor in resolving the matter peacefully.

While such immediate dissolutions are uncommon, similar incidents have been reported in parts of Uttar Pradesh where marriages arranged under family pressure were later called off after the bride or groom expressed unwillingness.

Authorities have urged families to prioritise consent and open communication to prevent such situations.

articles.title: Auto Driver Killed After Braking to Save Monkey in Jampenahalli
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a tragic road accident reported from Tumakuru district, an auto-rickshaw driver lost his life after applying sudden brakes to avoid hitting a monkey that was crossing the road. The incident occurred near Jampenahalli village in Koratagere.

body.html:
In a tragic road accident reported from Tumakuru district, an auto-rickshaw driver lost his life after applying sudden brakes to avoid hitting a monkey that was crossing the road.

The incident occurred near Jampenahalli village in Koratagere. The deceased has been identified as Mahendra Kumar, a resident of Sompura. He was travelling from Koratagere towards Tumakuru when the accident took place.

According to eyewitnesses and preliminary police findings, a monkey suddenly darted across the road. In an attempt to save the animal, Mahendra Kumar applied sudden brakes, causing the auto-rickshaw to lose balance and overturn.

Moments later, an Innova car approaching from the Tumakuru side rammed into the overturned auto. The collision impact was severe, leaving Mahendra Kumar critically injured.

He was rushed to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead despite efforts to save him.

Police have registered a case and launched an investigation to determine the exact sequence of events, including vehicle speed and road visibility conditions. Statements of the car driver and eyewitnesses are being recorded.

Authorities have urged motorists to exercise heightened caution on rural roads, particularly in areas prone to sudden animal crossings, to prevent similar tragedies.

articles.title: Property Greed Turns Deadly: Wife, Son Among 4 Arrested for Labourer’s Murder in Hirenandihalli
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: What initially appeared to be a mysterious death in a village in Karnataka has unravelled into a pre-planned murder allegedly driven by a property dispute. On February 20, villagers found a decomposed body in a maize field on the outskirts of Hirenandihalli village in Belagavi district.

body.html:
What initially appeared to be a mysterious death in a village in Karnataka has unravelled into a pre-planned murder allegedly driven by a property dispute.

On February 20, villagers found a decomposed body in a maize field on the outskirts of Hirenandihalli village in Belagavi district. Police initially registered a case of unidentified death. The deceased was later identified as 50-year-old Kalmesh Kotti, a native of the village who was working at a home care centre in Tumakuru. He had returned home for Maha Shivaratri.

Marital Discord and Loan Dispute

According to police, Kalmesh and his wife Kasturi had been living separately for nearly 12 years due to marital disputes. Kasturi was residing at her parental home in Kundagol along with their son.

Five years ago, Kasturi allegedly borrowed ₹8–9 lakh from her brother Mallesh Ammannavar for their daughter’s marriage, mortgaging Kalmesh’s three acres of ancestral land. However, disputes arose when Kalmesh reportedly refused to transfer the land documents or repay the loan.

Police said Kasturi allegedly conspired with her brother, believing that if Kalmesh died, the property would legally pass to her, enabling her to sell the land and clear the debt.

Murder Under Pretext of Party

Investigators revealed that on the night of February 16, Mallesh and his friend Mudukappa Kolekar allegedly took Kalmesh to a farmland under the pretext of a party. There, they allegedly strangled him with a rope.

To mislead investigators, the accused allegedly shifted the body to another field and attempted to stage it as a natural death. Police also stated that the body was found in a mutilated condition.

During sustained interrogation, police uncovered the alleged involvement of Kasturi and her son Kiran Kotti, who were reportedly aware of the conspiracy.

Arrests and Police Statement

The Kittur Police arrested Mallesh Ammannavar (32), Mudukappa Kolekar (30), Kasturi Kotti (42), and Kiran Kotti (25). All four have been remanded to Hindalga Central Jail.

Belagavi Superintendent of Police K. Ramarajan stated that the murder was a pre-planned act rooted in a property dispute. Further investigation is underway to examine all aspects of the case.
